messages:
Anya_Support: Escalation from FinOpsCo (org: finops-221). They report responses suddenly 'quieter' / more direct after our model bump on 2026-03-01 ~14:03 UTC. Customer says reply length and phrasing changed — examples attached. Asking for help to triage and a quick mitigation if needed. :eyes:

Sam_Dev: Thanks Anya. Can you paste the customer's example and the API request_id if available? Also which model they were routed to (if they provided it)?

Anya_Support: Customer supplied both. Sample input + two outputs they saved: 
---
User: "How do I reset my billing threshold?"
Prev (customer-captured): "Go to Account > Billing > Thresholds, click Reset, follow the prompts. If you'd like I can walk you through the steps or do it for you—happy to help!"
Now (after bump): "Account → Billing → Reset threshold. Done."
---
They also logged request_id: RQ-3321, timestamp 2026-03-01T14:05:02Z, model reported by SDK: "redwood-3.0-compact", temperature: 0.0, prompt_tokens: 256, response_tokens: 38. They said the behavior started right after our rollout window at ~14:00 UTC.

Mike_RnD: Interesting. Two quick hypotheses: (1) model variant difference — compact/quantized variants sometimes compress style and drop hedging/softeners; (2) config or sampling change (temp or top_p) — but you said temp=0.0 so that's already deterministic.

Luis_Oncall: I'm pulling routing logs for RQ-3321. One sec. :computer:

Luis_Oncall: Routing excerpt for RQ-3321: 
```
2026-03-01T14:05:02Z request=RQ-3321 org=finops-221 route=policy=fallback_cost selected_pool=compact-pool-2 model_variant=redwood-3.0-compact kernel=quant-int4 kv_cache=true
2026-03-01T14:05:02Z node=compact-node-12 cpu=09% gpu=81% pool_util=0.85
```
No rate limit or auth issue, it explicitly hit a fallback cost-driven route to the compact pool at time of rollout. We've got a handful of similar entries from that minute with same policy.

Anya_Support: Customer also attached a curl repro they ran. Posting it here so engineering can reproduce locally: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3.0-compact","input":"How do I reset my billing threshold?","temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":150}'
```
They get the terse output above consistently.

Sam_Dev: Good catch Luis — routing rule change during rollout likely the root cause. Two quick asks: can we A/B the compact vs the full-precision 3.0 on that prompt to confirm style delta? And can we temporarily pin finops-221 to full redwood-3.0 so the customer sees previous behavior while we investigate?

Mike_RnD: I'll run a small local eval now. Reproduced quickly: with redwood-3.0 (fp16) the model returns the longer, hedged answer. redwood-3.0-compact returns the shorter direct reply. Preliminary diff looks like compact has different tokenization behavior + a slightly different decode bias in the quantized kernel. I'll capture generated deltas and add to regression suite.

Luis_Oncall: I can patch their org routing to prefer pool=full-pool-1 for 24h. Doing change now and I'll monitor for errors. Pinned policy id: pol-9942.

Anya_Support: Customer accepted the pin. I've informed them we'll monitor and follow up in 1 hour.

Sam_Dev: Next steps for the team: 1) Mike to run controlled comparisons and save example pairs to the eval repo; 2) Engineering to add a regression test that flags style/verbosity deltas for model variants; 3) Ops to review routing rule that caused automatic cost-fallback during a full model rollout and consider safety guard for customer-facing orgs.

Mike_RnD: Action: I saved three paired examples to //evals/variant-style/finops-221-1999456789 (will link PR). Early note: compact tends to prune courtesy phrases at lower token budgets — even with same max_tokens — likely due to beam/penalty interplay in our quantized decoder.

Luis_Oncall: Pin applied. Snapshot: 
```
2026-03-01T14:09:10Z org=finops-221 policy=pol-9942 action=pin target=redwood-3.0 pool=full-pool-1
```
Monitoring: no error spikes.

Anya_Support: I'll send customer a recovery note: explain routing fallback, confirm pin, offer rollback window. Also capturing their example into the case for product notes. :white_check_mark:

Sam_Dev: If Mike's diff confirms behavioral regression in the compact kernel, product should decide whether to mark compact as 'not recommended' for support/UX-sensitive use-cases and update Optimize docs. Also add a quick check in release notes when we promote compact variants.

EvalBot: Auto-note: Created ticket INF-8672 for variant-style regression tracking and linked RQ-3321.

Anya_Support: Will update thread after 1h monitoring or if customer reports anything else. Thanks team. :pray:
